description: Born James Dell Collins in Round Rock; mother Tamara Causey separated from his biological father when he was seven weeks old; stepfather Mark Talarico later adopted him.

location: Wells Branch and Round Rock, Texas
description: Attended Wells Branch Elementary outside Austin per his official House biography; date range is approximate and not documented.
Attended McNeil High School; competed in speech and debate and played Danny Zuko in a production of Grease.
Earned a BA in government in 2011; organized students to lobby for tuition relief while an undergraduate.

organization: Teach For America; Rhodes Middle School
description: Joined Teach For America and taught sixth grade Language Arts at Rhodes Middle School on the West Side of San Antonio; the campaign describes him as a former middle-school teacher.
Earned a master's degree in education policy from Harvard.
Enrolled as a Presbyterian seminarian; the campaign and TIME describe him as a seminarian on academic leave rather than a graduate.
Announced a challenge to Republican incumbent Larry Gonzales in a district Trump carried; walked the entire 25-mile length of the district during the campaign.

role_or_event: Won Democratic primary for House District 52
description: Won the Democratic primary for HD-52 and went on to win the general election by fewer than 2,500 votes.
Won HD-52 in a district carried by Trump; reporting describes him as winning at age 28, while his Wikipedia record gives his age at swearing-in as 29.
Joined the House as its youngest member that session; helped write the school finance overhaul and establish the first Pre-K class-size cap.
Served on Public Education, Juvenile Justice and Family Issues, and Calendars during his House tenure.
Won the 2020 Democratic primary with about 51.5 percent and was re-elected in November.
Passed Javier Ambler's Law (HB 54) banning reality-TV policing contracts and carried the Narcan-on-campus legislation; voted against the transgender student-athlete bill.

role_or_event: Quorum break to block voting legislation
description: Left Texas with Democratic colleagues to deny a quorum in the first special session and block a restrictive voting bill; cites this on his campaign's anti-corruption page.
After the 2021 redistricting made his district more Republican, he ran in HD-50 and won re-election; criticized the maps as racist gerrymandering.

role_or_event: Proposed state constitutional amendment on abortion
description: Proposed an amendment preventing the Legislature from further restricting abortion access; the proposal was not adopted.

Sponsored SB 1145 creating a property-tax exemption for qualifying childcare facilities, led House opposition to private school vouchers, and carried HB 30 giving incarcerated minors a path to a high school diploma.
Filed a paid family leave bill, citing his mother being forced back to work days after his premature birth.
Filed a Pre-K class-size cap bill; a substantively similar 22-student cap was enacted through SB 2081.
Won re-election with roughly 63 percent of the vote.
Led House opposition to the Ten Commandments display requirement, fought the private school voucher bill, and proposed a second constitutional amendment protecting abortion.

role_or_event: Second quorum break during redistricting special sessions
description: Left the state with Democratic colleagues to block mid-decade redistricting maps; his campaign states he broke quorum twice.

role_or_event: Announced candidacy for the U.S. Senate
description: Announced a Senate campaign for the seat held by John Cornyn; launch timing is dated 2025-09-09 in his Wikipedia record and described only as September 2025 in campaign finance reporting.

role_or_event: Colbert interview and CBS/FCC censorship episode
description: Stephen Colbert alleged CBS was blocking an interview with Talarico; the interview posted to YouTube drew nearly 9 million views and helped raise $2.5 million in roughly 24 hours plus 4,000 volunteers.
Won the Democratic primary with about 52.4 percent against Jasmine Crockett, despite polls a week earlier showing him trailing by double digits.
Defeated Ken Paxton with 5,447,069 votes (55.06 percent) to Paxton's 4,250,664 (42.97 percent), becoming the first Democrat to win a statewide Texas race in roughly three decades.
